question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, the period is **six months** from the date the officer or employee was offered employment in the Institute.

- [621/2025 §33(2)(b)]: an officer/employee “who wishes to opt out of employment in the Institute, may do so **within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute**.”
- [621/2025 §33(2)(c)]: such an opting-out employee is then paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme approved by the Minister and the Finance Minister.

Caveats: The clause uses “offered employment,” not “notified,” as the start of the six-month period; no separate deadline from a notification date appears in the cited evidence.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer: Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded from subsection (2) if they were claimed “for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018” [013/2026 §37]. The same text also appears in 022/2026.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is valid for **one year** [645/2025 §25].

- The clause states it shall “be valid for a period of one year” and “specify the date of expiry” [645/2025 §25(c)–(d)].
- Caveat: this is the moneylending licence. A separate microfinance-business licence issued under section 32 is issued for a period of **three years** [645/2025 §32(7)].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect is **three years**, increased from two years.

- Section 8(2)(b) is amended by substituting “a period of two years” with **“a period of three years”** [033/2026 §9].
- The High Court’s earlier confirmation period is also changed from “shall not exceed three months” to **“shall not exceed four months”** [033/2026 §9].
- The initial police-issued freezing order is changed from seven days to **“fourteen working days”** [020/2026 §8].

Caveats: The three-year maximum appears in the 2026 Bill version; no GS counterpart for section 8 is included in the provided evidence.

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Licences granted **before** the new section takes effect give employees a three-year income tax exemption; licences granted **on or after** commencement make employees’ employment income taxable.

- Pre-commencement licence: for three years from the month after commencement, resident employees’ employment income “shall be exempt from income tax” and goes to a personal foreign currency account; non-resident employees are likewise exempt and not taxed on outside Sri Lanka income [654/2025 §3; 652/2025 §3].
- Post-commencement licence: resident and non-resident employees’ employment income “shall be liable to income tax” [654/2025 §3; 652/2025 §3].

The Bill and GS texts are identical on this point.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The bill amends the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005 by substituting scheduled words and making specific changes to sections 2A, 3, and 16A. [018/2026 §2]

- Section 2A(2) is replaced to extend the Act to certain extraterritorial terrorist acts, including acts against Sri Lankan citizens or government facilities. [018/2026 §3]
- Section 3’s proviso is replaced, participation bases are expanded, and a new subsection (2B) criminalises financing travel/training for terrorist purposes or becoming a “foreign terrorist fighter.” [018/2026 §4]
- Section 16A definitions are amended: “finance business” is repealed; new definitions include “armed conflict,” “computer data,” “computer system,” and “foreign terrorist fighter”; “funds or property” becomes “funds, property or other assets.” [018/2026 §16]

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
An investigation officer may, with Magistrate’s authorisation under §56, conduct these advanced investigative techniques: controlled delivery; digital surveillance, including interception/recording of digital, voice and video communication; undercover operations including use of decoys; laying of traps; and forensic extraction of data, information and images from computers, mobile phones, digital storage devices and other digital equipment [570/2025 §60(1)].

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five council members are required, and the Chairperson must be among them: the quorum is “five members including the Chairperson” [054/2026 §7(2)]. The Gazette version has the same requirement [040/2026 §7(2)].

- Meetings may be held in person or by audio-visual means where participants can simultaneously see and hear each other [054/2026 §7(3)].
- If the Chairperson is absent, the Vice-Chairperson presides; if both are absent, members elect someone to preside [054/2026 §7(5)].

Caveats: The quorum clause says “including the Chairperson,” which could create tension with the absence-presiding provisions; the text does not expressly address whether a meeting can be quorate if the Chairperson is absent.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?

- Each provider must prepare his fare list “in accordance with such lists published in such website” and display it “at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle”; the Commission may inspect, and non-compliance is “an offence under section 40” [577/2025 §19].

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
